Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a right-sided, lobulated soft-tissue density mass in the superior mediastinum that aligns with the esophageal course; this radiographic appearance, combined with symptoms of dysphagia and dyspepsia, is most consistent with an esophageal lipoma. Other options like lymphadenopathy or thymoma do not fit the specific combination of the lobulated morphology and gastrointestinal symptoms as well as a benign esophageal tumor.
